summary_paraphrased: Reviewer says Spotify recommendations feel surprisingly accurate, describing the algorithm as understanding their taste well across studying, relaxing, and various moods.

Reviewer reports no longer being able to play their own liked songs on demand, alongside inability to play albums in order, as part of broader free-tier restriction complaints; says they are planning to switch services.
Reviewer says free tier forces shuffle-only playback with no ability to choose a specific song or jump to a timestamp, calling it a frustrating limitation on control over listening.
Reviewer says playlists cannot run in their intended order due to forced shuffle on free tier, requiring manual song-by-song selection to get desired content.
Reviewer explicitly states recommendations are often repetitive, citing this as a core reason the app feels frustrating and poor value for free users.

Reviewer says the app constantly pushes unrequested podcasts/recommendations while burying songs they actually want; explicitly states the algorithm seems convinced they only want to hear the same handful of songs on repeat.

Long-time premium subscriber says recommendation algorithms have declined in quality, making it harder to find new music since the app keeps surfacing the same older content; also requests the return of a previously available curated BPM-based running playlist mix.

Long-time user reports it has become difficult to discover small/independent artists, with recommendations clogged by sponsored popular artists -- including some they had explicitly blocked -- and attributes a perceived decline in curation quality to layoffs and AI-generated playlist curation; says they will switch if a good alternative is found.

Reviewer says shuffle does not genuinely randomize, instead favoring recently played songs; separately states Discover Weekly is poorly tailored and rarely surfaces their actual genres, yielding only a handful of liked songs over time.
Reviewer with a 27-hour playlist reports the same songs repeat constantly despite the large pool of available tracks, describing it as actively harming their listening experience.

Reviewer reports a homescreen redesign removed most previously diverse suggested-playlist content (e.g. 'Made for You' sections), leaving only recently played items and unwanted autoplay snippets, with no way to disable the new format.

Reviewer expected 'Go to song radio' to surface genre/tempo-similar tracks but found it instead shuffles generic new releases, suggesting a mismatch between expected and actual recommendation logic for that specific feature.

Reviewer requests a true 'dislike' button distinct from the existing 'hide' function, arguing hidden songs still occupy playlist slots and the lack of negative feedback granularity limits the algorithm's ability to improve recommendations; also flags an unrelated DJ playback issue.

Reviewer is largely satisfied but specifically asks for an option to disable 'Smart Shuffle' when shuffling personal playlists, saying the existing Radio feature already adequately covers new-music discovery and that forced discovery-mixing into personal playlist shuffle is unwanted.
Reviewer without premium reports their playlist surfaces 'a bunch of the same people over and over' on shuffle, calling it annoying alongside other free-tier playback restrictions.

Reviewer states Spotify's 'Shuffle' functions more like a fixed playlist order than genuine randomization, noting that manually queueing a song doesn't update the underlying shuffle order, leading to possible immediate repeats.
Premium subscriber reports shuffle quality has degraded, now surfacing the same songs and artists repeatedly in sequence, undermining the core purpose of shuffle as a variety mechanism.

Reviewer claims that regardless of playlist size (cites a 4,000-song example), the app consistently defaults to replaying only the top ~40 most-played tracks, leaving the vast majority of a personal library effectively unheard.
Long-time user reports a broken shuffle feature as one of several technical/quality regressions experienced over years of use, alongside performance complaints.

Reviewer says the app frequently recommends music they actively dislike via what they describe as an unpredictable algorithm, citing this alongside other concerns as reasons for planning to leave the platform.

Reviewer notes Discover Weekly performance is inconsistent ('hit or miss') even on premium, while otherwise praising the platform's library and offline features; separately criticizes recent AI-related additions.
Reviewer states the recommendation algorithm frequently suggests content that is the opposite of what they actually listen to, and separately criticizes AI-generated playlist curation as low quality.

Reviewer acknowledges a strong music library but cites a newly introduced 6-skips-per-day limit (free tier) as a primary reason they are close to discontinuing use, framing restricted skip access as incompatible with relaxed listening.

Free-tier reviewer objects to skip limits and especially to unsolicited recommendation insertions into a manually curated playlist, explicitly stating they don't want automated additions to a playlist they built themselves; notes they eventually paid for premium but considers it barely worth the cost.
Reviewer's complaint centers on lost downloaded files, but separately the broader thread context reinforces a perception of declining reliability in core library/playlist features.

Reviewer specifically objects to the app inserting unrequested songs into a self-made playlist, asking rhetorically what the point of manual curation is if the system overrides it; cites this as a reason they may switch platforms.
